Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText:
I recently broke down and joined the ranks of a Weber owner. I am 40 years old and have always had the relatively cheap gas grills that last a few years. You know the ones – the 200.00 job at the hardware store that looks fantastic when you buy it. And it was! It cooked great for the first year. Then the 2nd year, it was ok. The 3rd year, you said to yourself “Well, I am going to rebuild the baby and get a few more years out of it!” 
Here is where you ran into your first issue – there were no parts to be found anywhere! The same hardware store is now selling the “updated” version. The parts don’t match and they want you to buy another grill. 
I looked over at the Weber grills and something caught my eye – a 10-year, top to bottom warranty! This can’t be true. I read the fine print, and sure enough, it is. Anything that breaks, outside of normal wear and tear, is covered. Ok – as Peter Griffin would say … “Keep going” … 
Next, I see all these parts on the wall at my local hardware store. There is a section for weber parts that is 4 times as big as the generic parts. I did not get the impression that “Weber’s were cheap because of all the replacement parts offered” I got the impression that, just like a car, you will need to replace items over time. And look! You can actually purchase them at a local hardware store! This means when something breaks, and your wife has 10 people coming over for an impromptu cookout – you can run to the store and get what you need. And bonus – these parts are reasonably priced! 
Ok – I bit. I bought the 3 burner Weber Spirit 2 in sapphire blue. Being a nerd, I read the owner’s manual cover to cover – I wanted to take care of my new investment. After burning it in for 20 minutes, I threw on some chicken. 
The first thing I noticed was how hot the grill got. I think it got up to around 550 degrees with the lid closed. I was worried I would not be able to wrangle this beast. I opened the lid and it cooled off quick. Superior cook box that hold in heat when needed and lets it go after. 
The grill cooks fantastic! The rear of the grill is hotter than the front consistently. This is by design and I like it. The 2 side tables are worth their weight in gold! Previously, I had a side burner I would never use. I went from a side burner to 2 sturdy side tables that I love. 
The components of the grill are top notch as well. The grates weigh about 5 pounds each, the lid closes quietly, and the overall structure of the grill is solid. It lights every time on the first try and grease is funneled down into a replaceable tin pan. It is clean, neat, and easy to maintain. 
If I were you, the next time your generic grill goes out, quit playing around. Buy a grownup grill that will last you awhile. Don’t take my word – do your research – ask your friends and google till there is no tomorrow. You will find that the little area in your mind that likes to grill will be very satisfied.
Results.Title: First time Weber owner

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText: I just picked this up this weekend after doing lots of research on the gas grill market. I was looking to get something of quality design without breaking the bank. I have a family of 4 so grilling space was a necessity. Purchased it assembled and once I got it home, was able to attach the LP tank and fire it up immediately. Heats to 500 degrees in less than 10 minutes. Solid design, feels sturdy, and looks great. Cons would be as others have mentioned - no handle for moving the grill, you have to use the shelf, which is very sturdy when attached properly; the wheels do seem pretty basic for the quality of the rest of the cart; and not being able to lower the right side shelf, which makes transporting a bit more challenging. Otherwise I am happy so far!
